intent.raw_query: Safari Kenya family of 3, $8000, 10 days, July 2026

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in a dramatic spectacle. Game drives through the Maasai Mara ecosystem offer sightings of the Big Five including lions, elephants, leopards, buffalos, and rhinos in their natural habitat.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views
experiences.description: Explore Amboseli National Park, home to some of Africa's largest elephant herds set against the stunning backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro. Guided game drives allow close encounters with massive elephant families, as well as cheetahs, giraffes, and hundreds of bird species in the swamp ecosystems.

experiences.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking
experiences.description: Visit Ol Pejeta Conservancy, home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth and the largest black rhino sanctuary in East Africa. Guided bush walks and game drives offer intimate wildlife encounters, and the conservancy's conservation story provides a deeply moving and educational nature experience.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Big Five Safari
experiences.description: Discover Lake Nakuru National Park, famous for its breathtaking flocks of pink flamingos coating the alkaline lake shores. The park also shelters Rothschild giraffes, white and black rhinos, lions, and leopards, making it one of Kenya's most diverse and photogenic wildlife destinations.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Tsavo East Red Elephant Bush Safari
experiences.description: Explore Kenya's largest national park, Tsavo East, renowned for its iconic red elephants dusted in volcanic soil, vast open savannahs, and the dramatic Galana River. Night game drives and guided bush walks reveal nocturnal predators, and the remote wilderness offers an authentic off-the-beaten-path safari experience.
experiences.location: Tsavo East National Park, Taita-Taveta County

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Kenya
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear immigration, collect baggage, and arrange budget airport transfer (matatu or shared shuttle) to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in and settle into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: N/A - in transit
meals.lunch: N/A - in transit
meals.dinner: Grab a light late-night snack at the airport or a nearby 24-hour local kiosk upon arrival. Budget: ~KES 300-500.

day_by_day.notes: Keep some Kenyan Shillings handy for transport from the airport. A shared shuttle or matatu from JKIA to the coast area costs significantly less than a private taxi. Confirm hotel late check-in in advance. Rest well for the adventure ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up and enjoy your first morning at the beachfront resort. Take a leisurely walk along the beach to get oriented with the surroundings. Explore the local area near the resort on foot, observing coastal birdlife and the warm Indian Ocean scenery. Look out for fish eagles and kingfishers common along the Kenyan coast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby local market to pick up fresh tropical fruits, snacks, and supplies for the trip. Interact with local vendors to get a feel for Kenyan coastal culture. Explore the surrounding neighborhood and look for budget tour operators offering safari packages.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxing sunset walk on the beach. Have dinner at a local 'mama mboga' (local food vendor) or a budget beachside restaurant serving fresh seafood and Kenyan staples.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort or a nearby local cafe serving mandazi (fried dough) and chai tea. Budget: ~KES 200-400.
meals.lunch: Fresh fruit from the local market plus a simple meal of ugali and sukuma wiki at a local canteen. Budget: ~KES 300-500.
meals.dinner: Grilled fish with coconut rice at a local beachside eatery. Budget: ~KES 500-800.

day_by_day.notes: July is dry season on the Kenyan coast with warm weather around 25°C — perfect for beach exploration. Exchange currency at a local forex bureau for better rates than airport counters. Start researching budget safari options for upcoming days.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning nature walk along the coastline or a nearby nature trail to spot coastal wildlife including monitor lizards, tropical birds, and crabs. Bring water and sunscreen. If near Mombasa, consider a budget matatu ride to Haller Park, a free-entry wildlife sanctuary with giraffes, hippos, and crocodiles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Haller Park (formerly Bamburi Nature Trail) in the afternoon for a self-guided wildlife walk. See rescued wildlife including Aldabra tortoises, hippos, and various antelope species in a natural setting. Entry fee is very affordable at approximately KES 500-800 for residents/budget travelers.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area by matatu. Stroll along the beach at dusk and enjoy the cooler evening breeze. Have dinner at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Chapati and eggs at a local roadside cafe. Budget: ~KES 150-300.
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic lunch from the local market — samosas, fruits, and a cold soda. Budget: ~KES 300-500.
meals.dinner: Swahili cuisine at a local restaurant — try pilau rice with beef or chicken. Budget: ~KES 500-700.

day_by_day.notes: Matatu rides are the most budget-friendly way to get around (KES 50-100 per ride). Haller Park is one of Kenya's best-kept budget wildlife secrets and is very family-friendly. Carry insect repellent for evening outings.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by budget bus or shared shuttle toward Tsavo East or Tsavo West National Park — one of the world's largest wildlife reserves and very accessible from the coast. Book a budget group day safari in advance through a local operator (costs approximately KES 3,000-5,000 per person including park entry and shared vehicle).
day_by_day.afternoon: Full afternoon game drive in Tsavo East National Park. Look for the famous 'red elephants' of Tsavo (elephants coated in red volcanic dust), lions, zebras, giraffes, buffalo, and over 500 bird species. The dry July season means animals congregate near water sources making sightings excellent.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the coast by shared transport. Arrive back at the resort by early evening. Relax on the beach and enjoy a well-earned dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort or grab a mandazi and tea before departure. Budget: ~KES 200-350.
meals.lunch: Pack a budget lunch box or buy snacks at a roadside stop en route. Budget: ~KES 400-600.
meals.dinner: Celebrate your first safari day with a slightly splurge-worthy dinner at a local Swahili restaurant. Try nyama choma (grilled meat). Budget: ~KES 700-1,000.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Tsavo safari at least 1-2 days in advance through a local budget operator. Group safaris split costs significantly. July is peak dry season in Tsavo — wildlife viewing is exceptional near Galana River and Aruba Dam. Bring binoculars if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Morning snorkeling or beach exploration near the resort area. The Kenyan coast has beautiful coral reefs accessible via budget boat trips (approximately KES 1,000-1,500 per person). Look for sea turtles, colorful reef fish, and starfish. Alternatively, explore a nearby mangrove forest on a guided walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby coastal nature reserve or marine park. Watamu Marine National Park or Mida Creek (depending on location) offers excellent birdwatching with migratory birds from Europe and Asia present in July. Mida Creek is free to enter and great for flamingos, herons, and kingfishers.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dhow cruise along the coast — a traditional wooden sailboat ride is a quintessential Kenyan coastal experience. Budget operators offer shared dhow rides for approximately KES 1,000-1,500 per person at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Fresh tropical fruit platter and chai at a local cafe. Budget: ~KES 250-400.
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled seafood at a beachside shack — try grilled prawns or octopus. Budget: ~KES 600-900.
meals.dinner: Simple home-style meal at a local restaurant — beans, rice, and vegetables (githeri). Budget: ~KES 300-500.

day_by_day.notes: July is an excellent month for marine wildlife on the Kenyan coast. Whale sharks are sometimes spotted offshore in July. Always negotiate prices with boat operators and agree on costs upfront. Apply reef-safe sunscreen to protect the coral ecosystem.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget bus or matatu to explore a nearby national reserve or community conservancy. Shimba Hills National Reserve near Mombasa is an excellent budget option (KES 215 entry for residents/budget travelers) and is home to the rare sable antelope, elephants, leopards, and beautiful coastal rainforest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Shimba Hills — visit the Sheldrick Falls within the reserve for a refreshing swim in a natural waterfall pool. The forest canopy walk and birdwatching here are spectacular with over 230 bird species recorded.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by matatu. Visit a local craft market to browse handmade Kenyan souvenirs — Maasai beadwork, wood carvings, and kikoi fabrics. Practice bargaining respectfully for fair prices.

meals.breakfast: Fried eggs, toast, and fresh juice at a local roadside cafe. Budget: ~KES 250-400.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from the resort or buy at a local canteen near Shimba Hills. Budget: ~KES 300-500.
meals.dinner: Local Kenyan buffet at a budget restaurant — try irio (mashed peas and potatoes) with beef stew. Budget: ~KES 500-700.

day_by_day.notes: Shimba Hills is one of Kenya's most underrated wildlife destinations and significantly cheaper than the major national parks. The forest is lush and beautiful in July. Wear long sleeves and trousers for the forest walk to protect against insects.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day trip to explore a local Maasai or Mijikenda village cultural experience near the coast. Many community-run cultural tourism programs offer authentic village visits for approximately KES 500-1,000 per person. Learn about traditional wildlife conservation practices, beekeeping, and local ecology.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local bird sanctuary or nature reserve close to the resort. Many coastal areas have community-managed bird hides and trails that are free or very low cost. Spend the afternoon birdwatching and photographing the diverse coastal birdlife.
day_by_day.evening: Relax on the beach for the final hours of daylight. Watch the sunset over the Indian Ocean. Have a leisurely dinner at the resort or a nearby restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Coconut mandazi and spiced chai at a local Swahili cafe. Budget: ~KES 200-350.
meals.lunch: Traditional Kenyan meal at the cultural village visit or a local canteen. Budget: ~KES 400-600.
meals.dinner: Pizza or pasta at a slightly more tourist-oriented but still budget-friendly beachside restaurant for variety. Budget: ~KES 600-900.

day_by_day.notes: Supporting community-run cultural tourism directly benefits local families. Always ask permission before photographing people. July evenings on the coast are pleasantly warm — perfect for beach dining.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning budget bus to Nairobi (approximately 8 hours from Mombasa, cost KES 800-1,200 by budget bus companies like Modern Coast or Easy Coach). Book tickets in advance. Enjoy the scenic drive through Tsavo, spotting wildlife from the road including elephants, giraffes, and zebras crossing near the highway.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Nairobi. Check into a budget hostel or guesthouse in the Westlands or Milimani area (approximately KES 1,500-2,500 per night for a dorm or budget single room). Visit the Nairobi Giraffe Centre in the afternoon — feed endangered Rothschild giraffes up close (entry approximately KES 1,000 for non-residents, less for residents).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Westlands or downtown Nairobi area on foot. Visit a local supermarket to stock up on snacks. Have dinner at a popular local restaurant in Nairobi.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before bus departure — mandazi and chai. Budget: ~KES 150-300.
meals.lunch: Packed snacks on the bus or stop at a roadside restaurant en route. Budget: ~KES 300-500.
meals.dinner: Nyama choma and ugali at a popular Nairobi local eatery like Carnivore's budget section or a local barbecue spot. Budget: ~KES 700-1,000.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Nairobi bus ticket 1-2 days in advance especially during July peak season. The Nairobi-Mombasa highway passes through Tsavo and wildlife sightings from the road are common — keep your camera ready. Store valuables securely in Nairobi.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Nairobi National Park for a morning game drive — the only national park in the world within a capital city. Entry is approximately KES 430 for East African residents or KES 3,000 for non-residents. Budget group game drives are available from the park gate. See lions, rhinos, giraffes, and zebras with the Nairobi skyline in the background — a unique wildlife experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust elephant orphanage near Nairobi National Park (free entry, donations welcome). Watch baby orphaned elephants being fed and learn about Kenya's anti-poaching conservation efforts. Afterward, visit the Karen Blixen Museum (entry KES 1,000) for a glimpse into colonial Kenyan history and the Out of Africa story.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Maasai Market in Nairobi (held at various locations on rotating days — check schedule). Browse and buy authentic Kenyan crafts, jewelry, and fabrics at negotiable prices. Have a final Nairobi dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full English breakfast at a budget Nairobi cafe or hostel. Budget: ~KES 400-600.
meals.lunch: Street food lunch near Nairobi National Park — samosas, roasted maize, and fresh juice. Budget: ~KES 300-500.
meals.dinner: Ethiopian or Indian cuisine at a budget Nairobi restaurant for variety — both cuisines are widely available and affordable. Budget: ~KES 600-900.

day_by_day.notes: The David Sheldrick elephant orphanage visiting hours are strictly 11:00 AM daily — plan accordingly. Nairobi National Park is best visited early morning when animals are most active. Keep your budget hostel's contact number handy for navigation.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Kenya — take a last walk through a local Nairobi neighborhood or visit Uhuru Park and Central Park for a peaceful green space experience. Visit a local coffee shop to try authentic Kenyan single-origin coffee. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at a local craft shop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport for departure. Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Take a final matatu or budget shuttle to the airport (KES 100-200 from central Nairobi).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Kenya with incredible memories of wildlife, nature, and coastal beauty. Reflect on the safari adventures, coastal wildlife, and cultural experiences of the past 10 days.

meals.breakfast: Final Kenyan breakfast — avocado on toast with a fresh passion fruit juice at a local Nairobi cafe. Budget: ~KES 400-600.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or a final street food meal near the city center. Budget: ~KES 400-700.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal.

day_by_day.notes: Nairobi traffic can be severe, especially during rush hour (7-9 AM and 4-7 PM). Allow extra travel time to the airport. Ensure you have no restricted wildlife products (ivory, coral, certain shells) in your luggage — Kenya has strict wildlife protection laws. Keep receipts for any wood carvings or crafts purchased. Safe travels!

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and meet your pre-arranged airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront accommodation. Rest and prepare for the adventure ahead.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: On the flight or at the airport
meals.dinner: Light snack or room service at Aegean Bliss Resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport pickup before arrival to avoid delays at night. Keep your travel documents and Kenya e-visa confirmation handy. Exchange some currency or withdraw Kenyan Shillings (KES) at the airport ATM.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort overlooking the beachfront. Take a gentle orientation walk around the resort grounds and nearby beach area to acclimate to the warm 25°C Kenyan weather.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local cultural center or market near your resort area to pick up essentials, souvenirs, and get a feel for Kenyan culture. Explore the local neighborhood, interact with vendors, and sample fresh tropical fruits from roadside stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset stroll along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy the warm evening breeze and watch the stunning Kenyan sunset over the Indian Ocean or landscape. Head back to the resort for a relaxed first full dinner in Kenya.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort - enjoy fresh tropical fruits, eggs, and local Kenyan tea or coffee
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a local mid-range restaurant near the resort - try Kenyan staples like ugali, sukuma wiki, and nyama choma
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort restaurant or a nearby mid-range coastal restaurant - sample Swahili-influenced seafood dishes like grilled tilapia or prawn curry

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day. Stay hydrated as the warm summer weather can be dehydrating. Apply sunscreen generously. Confirm all upcoming safari bookings and transfers with your tour operator.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure (5:30 AM) by road or chartered light aircraft to Maasai Mara National Reserve. Begin your Great Migration Safari with a dawn game drive. Witness the spectacular sight of millions of wildebeest, zebras, and Thomson's gazelles moving across the golden savannah in one of nature's greatest spectacles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue your Maasai Mara game drive after a packed bush lunch. Focus on the dramatic Mara River crossing zones where wildebeest brave crocodile-infested waters. Spot lions, cheetahs, leopards, and hyenas that follow the migration. Photography opportunities are exceptional in the warm afternoon light.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your mid-range tented camp in or near the Mara. Enjoy sundowner drinks on the camp veranda listening to the sounds of the African bush. Attend a brief evening briefing from your guide about the next day's game drive plan. Dinner around a campfire under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure, or breakfast at the tented camp upon arrival
meals.lunch: Packed bush lunch eaten in the vehicle or at a scenic picnic spot inside the Mara
meals.dinner: Three-course dinner at your Maasai Mara tented camp - expect hearty African-inspired cuisine with grilled meats, vegetables, and fresh bread

day_by_day.notes: The Great Migration peak season is July-August making this timing perfect. Bring binoculars, a good camera with zoom lens, and warm layers for early morning drives as it can be cool at dawn. Stay inside the vehicle during game drives unless instructed otherwise by your guide.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day immersion in Maasai Mara. Pre-dawn wake-up at 5:00 AM for a sunrise hot air balloon safari over the Mara (optional upgrade). Float silently above the plains watching elephants, giraffes, and wildebeest herds below. Land for a traditional champagne bush breakfast in the wilderness.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit an authentic Maasai village (manyatta) for a cultural experience. Meet Maasai warriors, learn about their traditional way of life, witness traditional dances, and browse handcrafted beadwork jewelry. Return to the Mara for an afternoon game drive focusing on big cat sightings.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell game drive through the Mara as the sun sets, casting golden light over the savannah. Look for nocturnal animals beginning their evening activity. Return to camp for a celebratory dinner. Share stories with fellow travelers around the campfire and enjoy traditional Kenyan storytelling from your guide.

meals.breakfast: Bush breakfast in the wild following the balloon safari, or full breakfast at the tented camp
meals.lunch: Lunch at the tented camp - fresh salads, grilled chicken, and Kenyan stews
meals.dinner: Special dinner at the camp with a traditional Kenyan menu including pilau rice, nyama choma, and mandazi dessert

day_by_day.notes: The hot air balloon safari is an additional cost (approx. USD 450-500) but is a once-in-a-lifetime experience highly recommended during migration season. Maasai village visits typically cost USD 20-30 per person. Respect cultural customs and ask permission before photographing community members.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure from Maasai Mara and transfer to Amboseli National Park (approximately 4-5 hours by road or 1 hour by light aircraft). En route, enjoy sweeping views of the Rift Valley. Arrive at Amboseli and check into your mid-range lodge. Begin afternoon game drive immediately upon arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Amboseli Elephant Watching Safari with the iconic snow-capped peak of Mount Kilimanjaro as your backdrop. Amboseli is home to some of Africa's largest and most studied elephant herds. Watch massive bull elephants, playful calves, and matriarchal family groups roaming the dusty plains. The afternoon light on Kilimanjaro is spectacular for photography.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at a scenic viewpoint with unobstructed views of Mount Kilimanjaro glowing pink and orange at dusk. Return to your lodge for dinner. Enjoy the peaceful sounds of the African bush from your lodge veranda before retiring for the night.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Maasai Mara camp before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a roadside mid-range restaurant en route, or packed lunch during transfer
meals.dinner: Dinner at your Amboseli lodge - enjoy a buffet featuring both international and Kenyan dishes, with fresh vegetables and grilled meats

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli is best visited in the morning and late afternoon when Kilimanjaro is most visible as clouds typically build around the mountain by midday. July is an excellent month with clear skies and dry conditions. Keep your camera ready for the iconic elephant-with-Kilimanjaro shot.

day_by_day.morning: Full day in Amboseli. Rise before dawn for the best Kilimanjaro views and a morning game drive through the Amboseli marshes and swamps fed by underground streams from Kilimanjaro. Spot hippos, pelicans, and hundreds of bird species in the wetland areas. Elephant families gather at the water sources creating extraordinary wildlife viewing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided walking safari (with armed ranger) through a designated area of Amboseli for a ground-level perspective of the ecosystem. Learn about animal tracks, medicinal plants, and the interconnected web of Amboseli's wildlife. Visit the Observation Hill for panoramic views across the entire park and spotting wildlife from above.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local Maasai community bordering Amboseli to learn how traditional herders coexist with wildlife. Witness traditional ceremonies and purchase authentic handmade crafts directly from artisans. Return to the lodge for a relaxed final dinner in Amboseli under a star-filled sky.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the lodge before the dawn game drive, followed by a fuller breakfast upon return
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Observation Hill with views over Amboseli plains
meals.dinner: À la carte dinner at the lodge restaurant - try the Kenyan lamb stew or fresh tilapia with coconut rice

day_by_day.notes: Walking safaris must be conducted with a licensed armed ranger and are typically arranged through your lodge. Amboseli is known for excellent elephant photography - the combination of red dust, marshes, and Kilimanjaro backdrop is uniquely spectacular. Observation Hill entry is included in park fees.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure from Amboseli and transfer to Ol Pejeta Conservancy in the Laikipia Plateau (approximately 4-5 hours). Arrive at Ol Pejeta and check into your mid-range accommodation. Begin with an orientation briefing about the conservancy's critically important conservation mission.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking Experience. Join expert trackers and rangers to track the world's last two northern white rhinos, Najin and Fatu, protected 24 hours a day by armed guards. Also track southern white rhinos and critically endangered black rhinos. Learn about the global rhino conservation crisis and Ol Pejeta's groundbreaking work.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Sweetwaters Chimpanzee Sanctuary within Ol Pejeta, the only place in Kenya where you can see chimpanzees. These rescued chimps from Central and West Africa have found sanctuary here. Evening game drive as the conservancy's lions, leopards, and hyenas become active. Dinner at the conservancy lodge.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Amboseli lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a mid-range restaurant en route or at the Ol Pejeta conservancy café upon arrival
meals.dinner: Dinner at your Ol Pejeta lodge - enjoy a three-course meal featuring locally sourced ingredients and Kenyan specialties

day_by_day.notes: Ol Pejeta is a private conservancy with separate entry fees in addition to accommodation. The northern white rhino viewing is a deeply moving and historically significant experience - only two remain on Earth. Photography is permitted but follow all ranger guidelines closely. The conservancy also supports community development programs you can learn about.

day_by_day.morning: Full day at Ol Pejeta Conservancy. Dawn game drive through the conservancy's diverse habitats including open grasslands, acacia woodlands, and riverine forests along the Ewaso Nyiro River. Spot the Big Five - lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo, and rhino - all found within Ol Pejeta's boundaries. The conservancy has the highest density of black rhinos in East Africa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Ol Pejeta research center to learn about cutting-edge conservation science including IVF programs attempting to save the northern white rhino from extinction. Afternoon game drive focusing on the vast buffalo herds and predator activity. The Laikipia Plateau offers a different, less-crowded safari experience compared to the Mara.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset game drive along the Ewaso Nyiro River watching hippos and crocodiles in the golden light. Enjoy sundowner drinks at a scenic riverside spot. Return to the lodge for a farewell dinner at Ol Pejeta. Prepare bags for the next day's transfer to Lake Nakuru.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the lodge before the dawn game drive
meals.lunch: Bush lunch served in the field by conservancy staff - a quintessential safari experience
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Ol Pejeta lodge - try the conservancy's signature dishes featuring locally raised Angus beef

day_by_day.notes: Ol Pejeta has strict conservation guidelines - no off-road driving to protect the ecosystem. The conservancy's work is partially funded by tourism so your visit directly contributes to saving endangered species. Consider making a donation to the northern white rhino fund. Night drives may be available for additional wildlife viewing.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Ol Pejeta and transfer to Lake Nakuru National Park (approximately 2 hours). Arrive at Lake Nakuru and check into your mid-range lodge. Begin your Lake Nakuru Flamingo and Big Five Safari immediately. The lake's alkaline waters support millions of lesser and greater flamingos creating a breathtaking pink shoreline visible from several kilometers away.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue your Lake Nakuru game drive along the lake shores and through the surrounding acacia forest and open grasslands. Lake Nakuru is one of Kenya's best parks for rhino sightings with both black and white rhinos. Spot lions resting in the acacia trees - a rare tree-climbing lion behavior. Look for Rothschild's giraffes, one of the most endangered giraffe subspecies.
day_by_day.evening: Climb to the Baboon Cliff viewpoint for a panoramic aerial view of the entire Lake Nakuru basin with the pink flamingo carpet visible below. Watch the sunset paint the Rift Valley in dramatic colors. Return to your lodge for dinner and an early night to prepare for the final safari day.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Ol Pejeta lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a mid-range restaurant in Nakuru town en route to the park, or at your lodge upon arrival
meals.dinner: Dinner at your Lake Nakuru lodge - enjoy Rift Valley specialties including fresh lake fish and local vegetables

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru's flamingo numbers fluctuate depending on water levels and algae growth. July typically offers excellent flamingo viewing. The park is compact and can be thoroughly explored in 1-2 days. Baboon Cliff is a must-visit for photography. The park is also home to pelicans, cormorants, and over 450 bird species making it a birder's paradise.

day_by_day.morning: Final dawn game drive at Lake Nakuru to catch the magical morning light on the flamingos and wildlife. Spend time at the lake shore watching pelicans and flamingos feed in the shallow waters. Visit the waterfall area in the southern section of the park for a refreshing natural spectacle. Return to the lodge for a final safari breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer back to Nairobi (approximately 2-2.5 hours). Upon arrival in Nairobi, visit the David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust Elephant Orphanage (if timing permits, visiting hours are 11:00 AM daily) to see rescued baby elephants being rehabilitated for release back into the wild. Stop at a reputable craft market like Utamaduni or City Market for final souvenir shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Nairobi at a quality mid-range restaurant celebrating an incredible 10-day Kenyan adventure. Transfer to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport for your departure flight. Reflect on the extraordinary wildlife encounters, landscapes, and cultural experiences of your Kenyan journey.

meals.breakfast: Full final safari breakfast at Lake Nakuru lodge - savor your last morning in the African bush
meals.lunch: Lunch at a popular mid-range Nairobi restaurant such as Carnivore Restaurant (famous for its nyama choma experience) or a local café
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a quality Nairobi restaurant - try Talisman Restaurant or a rooftop restaurant with city views for a memorable final meal

day_by_day.notes: David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust requires advance online registration for elephant visiting hour. Confirm your departure flight time and allow at least 3 hours for airport check-in and security. Keep some Kenyan Shillings for last-minute shopping and tips for guides and lodge staff. Tipping is customary and greatly appreciated - budget approximately USD 10-15 per day per guide.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Kenya Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in a dramatic spectacle. Game drives through the Maasai Mara ecosystem offer sightings of the Big Five including lions, elephants, leopards, buffalos, and rhinos in their natural habitat.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views
experiences.description: Explore Amboseli National Park, home to some of Africa's largest elephant herds set against the stunning backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro. Guided game drives allow close encounters with massive elephant families, as well as cheetahs, giraffes, and hundreds of bird species in the swamp ecosystems.

experiences.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking
experiences.description: Visit Ol Pejeta Conservancy, home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth and the largest black rhino sanctuary in East Africa. Guided bush walks and game drives offer intimate wildlife encounters, and the conservancy's conservation story provides a deeply moving and educational nature experience.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Big Five Safari
experiences.description: Discover Lake Nakuru National Park, famous for its breathtaking flocks of pink flamingos coating the alkaline lake shores. The park also shelters Rothschild giraffes, white and black rhinos, lions, and leopards, making it one of Kenya's most diverse and photogenic wildlife destinations.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Tsavo East Red Elephant Bush Safari
experiences.description: Explore Kenya's largest national park, Tsavo East, renowned for its iconic red elephants dusted in volcanic soil, vast open savannahs, and the dramatic Galana River. Night game drives and guided bush walks reveal nocturnal predators, and the remote wilderness offers an authentic off-the-beaten-path safari experience.
experiences.location: Tsavo East National Park, Taita-Taveta County

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight UA arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Late arrival at Nairobi airport. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Welcome drink and light refreshments upon check-in. Settle into your beachfront suite and unwind after the long journey.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or at departure airport
meals.lunch: In-flight or at departure airport
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome platter and curated cheese & charcuterie board arranged by the resort upon arrival — paired with a glass of Kenyan craft gin or sparkling wine

day_by_day.notes: Ensure your resort is notified of the late arrival in advance. A dedicated butler or concierge should be on hand to assist with luggage and room orientation. No early wake-up required for Day 2 — allow for a leisurely start to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort's signature beachfront restaurant. Take a gentle orientation walk along the private beach with a resort naturalist who will introduce you to the coastal ecosystem, local birdlife, and marine environment. Warm summer weather at 25°C makes this a perfect gentle introduction to Kenya's natural beauty.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided snorkeling or glass-bottom boat excursion along the Kenyan coastline to explore coral reefs and tropical marine life. Return to the resort for a rejuvenating spa treatment at the luxury wellness center — choose from a traditional Swahili massage or a hot stone therapy session overlooking the Indian Ocean.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails on the private beach deck as the sun sets over the ocean. Enjoy a premium dinner at the resort's fine-dining restaurant featuring fresh Swahili coastal cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Lavish buffet breakfast at the resort's beachfront restaurant — fresh tropical fruits, eggs cooked to order, smoked fish, and Kenyan chai
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — grilled lobster, avocado salad, and freshly squeezed passion fruit juice
meals.dinner: Seven-course tasting menu at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant featuring Swahili-spiced prawns, coconut fish curry, and mango sorbet — paired with curated wines

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and acclimatization day. Weather is warm and pleasant at 25°C with minimal rain expected. Sunscreen and a light hat are recommended for outdoor activities. Confirm all upcoming safari logistics with the resort concierge today.

day_by_day.morning: Early private charter flight from the coast to the Maasai Mara region. Upon arrival, transfer by luxury 4x4 Land Cruiser to your exclusive tented camp. Begin the iconic Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari — witness millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles thundering across the savannah in one of nature's greatest spectacles. A private guide and open-roof vehicle ensure unobstructed wildlife viewing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Great Migration game drive, positioning near the Mara River to potentially witness dramatic river crossings where crocodiles await. Your expert guide will share deep ecological insights about this extraordinary annual event. Stop for a gourmet bush picnic lunch set up by camp staff in a scenic location.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the luxury tented camp for sundowner drinks on the camp's elevated viewing deck overlooking the plains. Freshen up before a candlelit bush dinner under the stars accompanied by Maasai cultural storytelling.

meals.breakfast: Continental breakfast at the resort before the early flight — pastries, fresh fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet bush picnic in the Mara — artisan sandwiches, cold meats, Kenyan cheeses, fresh fruit, and chilled beverages served on linen by camp staff
meals.dinner: Three-course candlelit dinner at the luxury tented camp — roasted game meat, seasonal vegetables, and a decadent chocolate fondant, paired with South African wines

day_by_day.notes: Pack a light jacket as Maasai Mara mornings and evenings can be cool. July is peak Great Migration season — this is the absolute best time to witness river crossings. Binoculars and a quality camera with a zoom lens are strongly recommended. All game drives use private vehicles with certified expert guides.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for an exclusive hot air balloon safari over the Maasai Mara at sunrise — drift silently above the golden savannah as lions, elephants, and migrating herds move below. This is a once-in-a-lifetime perspective of the African wilderness available only to a small number of guests per flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the balloon lands, enjoy a traditional champagne bush breakfast in the field. Return to camp for a brief rest, then embark on a guided walking safari with a Maasai ranger — learn to track wildlife on foot, identify plants used in traditional medicine, and gain an intimate ground-level connection with the ecosystem.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a traditional Maasai village (manyatta) for a private cultural immersion experience — witness traditional dances, learn about Maasai customs, and interact with community elders. Return to camp for a luxury spa treatment followed by a private dinner.

meals.breakfast: Champagne bush breakfast in the field following the hot air balloon landing — scrambled eggs, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, tropical fruits, and Moët & Chandon champagne
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the luxury tented camp — grilled chicken, quinoa salad, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Private dining experience at the camp — slow-braised lamb shank, roasted root vegetables, and a selection of East African desserts

day_by_day.notes: The hot air balloon safari must be booked well in advance and is weather-dependent. Flights typically last 60–90 minutes. Wear warm layers for the early morning balloon flight as temperatures at altitude can be cool. The Maasai village visit is a premium community-based tourism experience that directly benefits local families.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise game drive in the Maasai Mara focusing on predator activity — lions, cheetahs, and leopards are most active in the early morning hours. Your private guide will use expert tracking skills and radio networks to locate big cat sightings across the reserve.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private charter flight from Maasai Mara to Amboseli National Park. Check into a luxury lodge with iconic views of Mount Kilimanjaro. Begin the Amboseli Elephant Watching experience — Amboseli is home to some of Africa's largest and most studied elephant herds, with the snow-capped peak of Kilimanjaro providing a breathtaking backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset game drive in Amboseli as elephant families return to the swamps. Kilimanjaro is often clearest in the late afternoon light, offering extraordinary photographic opportunities. Return to the lodge for a premium dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full cooked breakfast at the Mara tented camp — eggs, bacon, fresh juice, and Kenyan coffee before departure
meals.lunch: In-flight snack box on the charter flight and light refreshments upon arrival at the Amboseli lodge
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Amboseli lodge's fine-dining restaurant — pan-seared tilapia, Kenyan vegetable stew, and a passion fruit panna cotta, paired with premium wines

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli in July offers exceptional elephant viewing as herds congregate around the park's permanent swamps. The chance of clear Kilimanjaro views is highest in the morning and late afternoon. Bring a telephoto lens for elephant photography. The charter flight between Mara and Amboseli takes approximately 45–60 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day deep immersion into the Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views experience. Morning game drive focusing on elephant family dynamics — observe matriarchs leading their herds, calves playing in the swamp, and bulls sparring on the open plains. Your guide will share insights from decades of elephant behavioral research conducted in Amboseli.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Amboseli Research Centre for a private briefing with a resident elephant researcher — learn about individual elephant identification, family histories, and conservation challenges. Afternoon game drive through the acacia woodlands and observation hill for panoramic park views.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private dinner set up in the bush with a direct view of Kilimanjaro as the mountain glows in the fading light — a truly magical fine-dining experience under the African sky with personal chef and butler service.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise breakfast at the lodge's outdoor terrace with Kilimanjaro views — fresh fruit, granola, eggs, and Kenyan single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch near the Amboseli swamps — smoked meats, artisan breads, salads, and chilled drinks
meals.dinner: Private bush dinner under the stars — five-course menu featuring Kenyan-inspired cuisine, paired with premium South African and French wines, with personal chef and butler

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli's swamps attract extraordinary birdlife in addition to elephants — over 600 bird species have been recorded. Bring a bird identification guide if interested. The private bush dinner must be pre-arranged with the lodge concierge and is weather-dependent.

day_by_day.morning: Private charter flight from Amboseli to Ol Pejeta Conservancy in Laikipia. Check into a luxury conservancy lodge. Begin the extraordinary Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking experience — this is home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth, Najin and Fatu, and the largest black rhino sanctuary in East Africa. A private ranger and tracker guide you on an intimate rhino encounter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exclusive access to observe Najin and Fatu, the world's last northern white rhinos, under the care of their dedicated 24-hour armed guard team. This is one of the most emotionally powerful and historically significant wildlife encounters on the planet. Continue with a game drive to track black rhinos and the conservancy's impressive lion and cheetah populations.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks in the bush followed by a guided night game drive — Ol Pejeta is one of the few conservancies offering exceptional night safaris where nocturnal species such as aardvark, porcupine, and bush babies can be spotted.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Amboseli lodge before departure — continental spread with hot options
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at the Ol Pejeta luxury lodge — grilled meats, fresh salads, and tropical fruit
meals.dinner: Dinner at the lodge's restaurant — slow-cooked beef tenderloin, roasted vegetables, and a rich chocolate mousse, paired with Kenyan craft beers and fine wines

day_by_day.notes: The encounter with Najin and Fatu is a deeply moving conservation experience. Guests are asked to maintain respectful distances and follow ranger instructions at all times. Photography is encouraged as a means of raising global awareness. Ol Pejeta also supports chimpanzee sanctuary — a brief visit can be arranged as an add-on.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive in Ol Pejeta focusing on the big cats — the conservancy has a thriving lion and cheetah population. Visit the conservancy's wildlife tracking center to learn about cutting-edge GPS collar monitoring and anti-poaching technology used to protect rhinos and other endangered species.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private charter flight from Ol Pejeta to Lake Nakuru. Check into a luxury lodge on the rim of the Great Rift Valley with panoramic views over the lake. Begin the Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Big Five Safari — the lake's alkaline waters host hundreds of thousands of pink flamingos creating a breathtaking pink carpet across the water's surface.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset game drive along Lake Nakuru's shores — spot white rhinos, Rothschild's giraffes, and large buffalo herds in the golden evening light. Return to the lodge for a celebratory dinner marking the halfway point of the safari journey.

meals.breakfast: Full cooked breakfast at the Ol Pejeta lodge before the morning game drive
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the lodge before the afternoon charter flight
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at the Lake Nakuru luxury lodge — Rift Valley lamb chops, grilled lake tilapia, and a decadent dessert platter with Kenyan coffee and liqueurs

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru's flamingo numbers fluctuate with water levels and algae blooms — July typically offers excellent flamingo viewing. The lake is also a sanctuary for both black and white rhinos. Binoculars are essential for birdwatching. The Rift Valley views from the lodge are spectacular at sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Lake Nakuru Big Five Safari experience. Morning game drive along the lake's forested edges — Lake Nakuru is one of Kenya's most reliable parks for leopard sightings as they rest in the yellow fever trees. Also look for lions, black and white rhinos, and the park's famous Rothschild's giraffes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon game drive focusing on the lake's extraordinary birdlife — in addition to flamingos, over 450 bird species have been recorded including pelicans, African fish eagles, and marabou storks. Stop at Makalia Falls within the park for a scenic bush walk. Private charter flight from Lake Nakuru back to the Kenyan coast in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort for the final nights of the trip. Enjoy a relaxing welcome-back dinner at the resort's beach restaurant as the waves of the Indian Ocean provide a soothing soundtrack after an intense week of safari adventures.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise breakfast at the Lake Nakuru lodge — fresh fruit, yogurt, eggs, and Kenyan tea
meals.lunch: Gourmet bush lunch in Lake Nakuru National Park — prepared and served by lodge staff in a scenic lakeside location
meals.dinner: Seafood dinner at the Aegean Bliss Resort beach restaurant — grilled whole fish, tiger prawns, and coconut rice, paired with crisp white wine

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru's Big Five status makes it one of Kenya's most rewarding parks for concentrated wildlife viewing. The afternoon charter flight back to the coast takes approximately 1–1.5 hours. Arriving back at the resort by early evening allows for a relaxing final stretch of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy a leisurely breakfast on your private terrace or the beachfront restaurant. Take a final sunrise beach walk to soak in the beauty of the Kenyan coast. Optional: arrange a private yoga or meditation session with the resort's wellness instructor on the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a final luxury spa session at the resort — choose from a full-body Swahili wrap, aromatherapy massage, or couple's treatment. Enjoy a last swim in the Indian Ocean or resort infinity pool. Visit the resort's boutique for premium Kenyan souvenirs — locally crafted jewelry, Maasai beadwork, and single-origin Kenyan coffee to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner at the resort's finest restaurant — a multi-course celebration of Kenyan cuisine and your extraordinary 10-day journey through one of Africa's greatest wildlife destinations. Toast to an unforgettable trip with premium Kenyan sparkling wine.

meals.breakfast: Lavish final breakfast at the resort — made-to-order eggs, smoked salmon, tropical fruit platters, fresh pastries, and specialty Kenyan single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Light poolside farewell lunch — grilled lobster tail, avocado and mango salad, and a glass of chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Premium farewell dinner at the resort's signature restaurant — seven-course Kenyan tasting menu featuring coastal and savannah-inspired dishes, paired with a curated wine flight and ending with a personalized dessert

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure flight details and arrange private airport transfer through the resort concierge. Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in and security. Pack any wildlife souvenirs carefully — ivory, certain animal products, and some plant materials are prohibited for export under CITES regulations. Keep all safari receipts and conservancy permits as memorable keepsakes of this extraordinary journey.
